newsitem.title: CHINA: No recovery seen in 1997 in China car market.
newsitem.headline: No recovery seen in 1997 in China car market.

text.p: China's car market in 1997 will be plagued by overproduction, slack demand and weak prices as in 1996, the Business News reported on Wednesday.

It will be hard to reach the planned 1996 output of 1.5 million cars, including 350,000 passenger cars, against an actual 1.503 million in 1995, with stockpiles expected to reach about 200,000 at the end of 1996, it said.
The planned output for 1997 is two million cars, it said.
Demand from state organisations and commercial companies will grow slightly in 1997 over the 1996 level, while demand by private individuals will remain small, it said.
It estimated total 1996 demand at 1.66 million cars and said prices were likely to remain at the level of early 1996. It gave no more details.
